findings.title: endpoint of the passive return
findings.claim: The passive return is directed toward a named endpoint, so the movement is not an unspecified displacement.
findings.mechanism: The preposition ila is the required complement of yuraddu and joins the passive return to rabbihi, converting return into movement toward a destination and jurisdiction.
findings.reader_payoff: The return acquires a visible destination before the ayah names the authority at that destination.
findings.containment: This establishes directed endpoint scope; it does not by itself specify the agent of return or replace the ayah's ordinary passive translation.

epistemic.reason: QAC alignment and trusted word-analysis supports directly supply the preposition's attachment and endpoint effect.

findings.title: personal Lord as transfer endpoint
findings.claim: The returned wrongdoer is directed to his own Lord, making the endpoint a personally specified relation rather than an abstract destination.
findings.mechanism: The construct rabb with the possessive suffix in rabbihi makes the destination definite through the wrongdoer's pronoun, and its placement before the final verb supplies the named authority for the next action.
findings.reader_payoff: The endpoint is heard as a relation belonging to the wrongdoer himself, and the following action has a named subject available in the sentence.
findings.containment: The noun names the personal Lord relation and does not narrate a new act of nurturing or settle every theological implication of Lordship.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis and QAC occurrence evidence directly support the construct relation, suffix, and local subject availability.

findings.title: immediate result after return
findings.claim: The second fa presents the Lord's punishment as the direct consequence after the return, without the future buffer attached to the first punishment.
findings.mechanism: Fa follows thumma and directly attaches to yuʿadhdhibuhu, while the first fa is fused with sawfa; the parallel consequence links therefore preserve a schedule only in the first clause.
findings.reader_payoff: After the transfer, the sentence moves straight into the Lord's action instead of inserting another scheduling word.
findings.containment: The contrast concerns local connective timing and does not claim that the first punishment is uncertain or that the second is temporally instantaneous in every sense.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis supports identify the second fa's attachment and its contrast with the first fa plus sawfa.

findings.title: divine punishment repeats the verb with changed subject
findings.claim: The punishment verb returns after the transfer with the same wrongdoer as object but with singular agency supplied by rabbihi.
findings.mechanism: The active Form II singular yuʿadhdhibuhu repeats the punishment-root action after the first-person plural nuʿadhdhibuhu, and the same third-person object suffix keeps the wrongdoer in view while agency changes.
findings.reader_payoff: The repeated verb is heard as a changed-authority action rather than as an accidental repetition.
findings.containment: The local subject is recovered from the named Lord relation; this does not infer an unstated agent for the passive return or add a doctrine of delegated authority.

epistemic.reason: Trusted morphology, attachment, and word-analysis supports supply the voice, number, subject relation, and repeated object.

findings.title: cognate noun opens the closing coda
findings.claim: The final clause expands from the divine punishment verb into a named, indefinite ordeal that the adjective can qualify.
findings.mechanism: The cognate accusative ʿadhaban names the result of yuʿadhdhibuhu and heads the adjective nukran, so the divine clause becomes fuller than the verb alone.
findings.reader_payoff: The sentence does not stop at the act of punishing; it makes the punishment itself an object of perception and qualification.
findings.containment: The noun is a cognate result and not a second independently timed punishment event; its indefiniteness is retained without adding a quantity claim.

epistemic.reason: Trusted attachment evidence identifies the cognate accusative and its adjective relation.

findings.title: final adjective makes the punishment uncatalogued
findings.claim: The closing adjective makes the named punishment severe and beyond ordinary recognition.
findings.mechanism: Nukran agrees accusatively and indefinitely with ʿadhaban; its n-k-r field joins terribleness with the quality of what is not recognized or ordinarily known, while the adjective remains a qualifier rather than a separate denial event.
findings.reader_payoff: The final landing becomes an ordeal that cannot be comfortably placed in the reader's ordinary catalogue of punishments.
findings.containment: This preserves both severity and strangeness as qualities of the punishment; it does not claim an act of denying, disguising, or mutually failing to recognize.

epistemic.reason: Trusted adjective analysis and the accepted focus branch for non-recognition support the bounded quality reading.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Tanınan ve belirli olanın karşıtı olarak tanınmayan ya da belirsiz olan.
branch_activations.carrier: The adjective nukran carries the branch's quality of what is not recognized or definite.

branch_activations.activation: Because nukran qualifies the named punishment noun, the non-recognition quality attaches to the ordeal itself rather than becoming an independent act.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The final punishment is an ordeal outside ordinary recognition as well as a severe punishment.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch is used for the punishment's quality; it does not introduce denial, disguising, or reciprocal failure to recognize.

findings.title: direct ruling speech opens the verdict
findings.claim: Qala opens the response as a completed, voiced ruling rather than an unframed reaction.
findings.mechanism: The active perfect speech verb governs the following conditional-punishment sequence as a settled declaration, giving the sentence a direct-speech frame.
findings.reader_payoff: The answer arrives as an articulated judgment with a speaker behind its ordered consequences.
findings.containment: The form supports a declaration frame; it does not exclude every possible discourse context or turn the local ruling into a broader speech genre.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis and QAC occurrence evidence support the active perfect speech act and its local governance.

findings.title: first branch of the case split
findings.claim: Amma marks this as the first side of a paired conditional distribution.
findings.mechanism: The topic-conditional particle is answered by the following fa and holds the man ẓalama clause as one branch, so the punishment statement is linked to a case frame rather than left free-floating.
findings.reader_payoff: The ruling begins with a visible distribution: this offender class receives its own stated consequence.
findings.containment: Only the local first-side framing is claimed; the other side is not imported as evidence or used to displace this ayah's content.

epistemic.reason: Trusted particle analysis and local answer attachment directly support the conditional topic frame.

findings.title: open wrongdoer class with suffix chain
findings.claim: Man leaves the offender class open and then tracks the same person through later object and possessive suffixes.
findings.mechanism: The indefinite relative-conditional pronoun is the subject of ẓalama, while later -hu and -hi forms resume that referent, so judgment attaches to whoever commits the act rather than to a named group.
findings.reader_payoff: The ayah's subject remains reusable: the person is identified by the wrongdoing and followed through every later stage.
findings.containment: The open class is a local syntactic effect and does not by itself quantify the population or settle the scope of wrongdoing beyond the conditional construction.

epistemic.reason: Trusted pronoun analysis, suffix tracking, and local attachment evidence support the open person-class.

findings.title: objectless completed wrong defines the branch
findings.claim: Ẓalama states completed active wrongdoing without naming a victim, making conduct itself the condition for the ruling.
findings.mechanism: The active perfect objectless verb under man identifies the offender through the completed act; the root's misplacement and darkness pressure remains coloring while the local form selects moral wrongdoing.
findings.reader_payoff: The sentence classifies by what a person has done without narrowing the ruling to one specified injured party.
findings.containment: This does not deny that wrongdoing can have victims or concrete objects elsewhere; it records only the objectless local syntax and selected moral sense.

epistemic.reason: Trusted active-form, object-status, and lexical analysis directly support the conduct condition and its boundary.

findings.title: required answer with delayed execution
findings.claim: The first fa answers amma at the level of clause linkage while sawfa defers the actual punishment.
findings.mechanism: Fa is the required answer and consequence particle fused with sawfa; the conditional result begins grammatically at once, but the future particle schedules nuʿadhdhibuhu.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish the sentence's immediate ruling structure from the later timing of its enactment.
findings.containment: The claim concerns grammatical consequence and scheduling together; it does not make the punishment immediate in execution or remove its certainty.

epistemic.reason: Trusted particle analysis and local answer attachment support both the required fa and its fusion with sawfa.

findings.title: scheduled first punishment
findings.claim: The first punishment is declared as the consequence but placed on its own future schedule.
findings.mechanism: The independent future particle sawfa scopes over the first-person plural punishment verb and its object suffix before the thumma transfer, separating verdict from execution.
findings.reader_payoff: The sentence gives the first sanction a definite place in the future rather than presenting it as already enacted.
findings.containment: This is a local tense-aspect and sequencing claim; it does not infer a duration, cause, or cancellation of the promised punishment.

epistemic.reason: Trusted QAC morphology and word-analysis support directly supply sawfa's scope and deferred-action effect.

findings.title: bounded human punishment stage
findings.claim: The first punishment is bounded as a first-person plural action against the same wrongdoer before the case leaves that jurisdiction.
findings.mechanism: Nuʿadhdhibuhu carries first-person plural agency and a third-person object suffix under sawfa; its position before thumma limits this action to the opening punishment stage.
findings.reader_payoff: The first sanction has an identifiable acting side and target before the sentence changes authority.
findings.containment: Plural agency is preserved without deciding whether it is human, delegated, or institutional beyond the supplied form and local reading.

epistemic.reason: Trusted form, agreement, and attachment evidence supply the agency, target, schedule, and stage boundary.

findings.title: interval before transfer to higher jurisdiction
findings.claim: Thumma inserts a marked interval between the first punishment and the return to the Lord.
findings.mechanism: Unlike the two fa links that answer and resume consequence tightly, thumma stands before passive yuraddu as a delayed-sequence connector, making the sentence cross a jurisdictional stage.
findings.reader_payoff: The transfer is felt as a real turn in the sentence rather than as another item in a flat list.
findings.containment: The interval is a relation of sequence and authority in this ayah; it does not assign an external legal hierarchy or a measurable duration.

epistemic.reason: Trusted connective analysis and local sequencing support distinguish thumma from the surrounding fa particles.

findings.title: passive transfer of the wrongdoer
findings.claim: Yuraddu makes the wrongdoer the passive subject of a directed return, while the returning agent remains unnamed.
findings.mechanism: The passive imperfect Form I places the tracked wrongdoer in the returned position and waits for ila to specify the destination; the root's return pressure is therefore realized as forced transfer rather than self-directed movement.
findings.reader_payoff: The wrongdoer stops acting in the sentence and is visibly carried toward the next authority.
findings.containment: The claim does not identify the hidden agent or turn the root's rejection and restoration possibilities into additional events.

epistemic.reason: Trusted QAC morphology, passive attachment, and word-analysis evidence directly support the returned subject and unnamed agent.

findings.title: two punishment stages
findings.claim: The ayah stages punishment in two jurisdictions: an initial sanction, then a return to the wrongdoer's Lord for a second punishment.
findings.mechanism: The repeated punishment action is interrupted by passive yuraddu ila rabbihi; thumma marks the later stage and the following fa resumes consequence after the return.
findings.reader_payoff: The repeated punishment verb becomes a transfer-and-return sequence rather than one undifferentiated penalty.
findings.containment: This is an attributed exact-focus HFT reading and does not erase the primary account of punishment or establish a legal taxonomy beyond the sentence.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace is exact to the supplied focus ayah and its branch/root coordinates, but the reader identity is legacy_unbound and the trace remains attributed.
